violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands: EMPLOYEE ARRANGING HAIR BEFORE WEARING HAT PROCEEDED TO ENGAGE IN FOOD PREPARATION ACTIVITIES WITHOUT WASHING HANDS.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEE TO WASH HANDS BEFORE RESUMING FOOD PREPARATION. PLEASE ENSURE EMPLOYEES TRAINING AND COMPLIANCE.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: Observed the handsink at the END OF COOK LINE being used TO WASH UTENSILS AND CLOTHS.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEES TO USE 3 COMPARTMENT SINK TO CLEAN AND SANITIZE UTENSILS AND WASHING CLOTHS.

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at handwashing sink IN SUSHI AREA AND IN BACK KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. PIC SUPPLIED PAPER TOWELS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE ALL HANDWASH SINKS ARE PROPERLY SUPPLIED.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: RAW SEAFOOD STORED ABOVE PREPARED VEGETABLES AND SAUCES; RAW CHICKEN STORED ABOVE BEVERAGES IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC REORGANIZED FOODS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

violations.title: Before Use After Cleaning
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment were not observed sanitized: POTS, PAN AND UTENSILS BEING WASHED AND RINSED IN 3 COMPARTMENT SINK WITHOUT SANITIZING; UTENSILS WASHED AT HANDWASHING SINK.
violations.corrective_action: All utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use and after cleaning. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEES TO TRANSFER KITCHENWARE TO DISHWASHING MACHINE FOR CLEANING AND SANITIZING DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: FRIED CRAB AT 79F ON COUNTER IN SUSHI STATION.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC WILL USE TPHC PROCEDURES AND DISCARD UNUSED PORTIONS AT 8:00PM. EHS WILL UPDATE TPHC DOCUMENTATION TO INCLUDE CRAB AND FORWARD TO PIC. Yaki Sushi (Inspection Date: 07/21/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name: CLEANING CHEMICAL SPRAY BOTTLES IN BACK KITCHEN WITHOUT LABELS.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEE TO APPLY LABELS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: WORKING CONTAINERS OF VARIOUS SAUCES, OILS, ETC IN SUSHI STATION AND MAIN KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEE TO APPLY LABELS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: RICE SCOOPS IN WATER AT 73F ON COUNTER.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EMPLOYEE REPLACED UTENSILS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE UTENSILS AE STORED ON CLEAN SANITIZED DRY SURFACE OR IN WATER AT 135F OR ABOVE. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk crate(s) found used for the following purpose(s): STORE FOODS IN BACK KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE PROVIDE APPROVED SHELVING OR DUNNAGE RACKS TO STORE FOODS AT LEAST 6 INCHES OFF THE FLOOR.

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition

violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods while it is not operating properly. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO REMOVE TCS FOODS FROM UNIT DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE DO NOT STORE TCS FOODS IN UNIT UNTIL REPAIRED AND CAN MAINTAIN FOOD TEMPERATURES AT 41F OR BELOW. EMAIL EHS ONCE REPAIR HAS BEEN COMPLETED.

violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE CLEAN AND IMPLEMENT AN APPROPRIATE CLEANING SCHEDULE.

violations.title: Food Protection Manager - Accredited Program
violations.observation: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager who has shown proficiency through passing an accredited examination. OBSERVED NO CFM ON SITE AT START OF INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: Obtain a certified food managers certificate from an accredited program. CFM ARRIVED DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE A CFM IS ON SITE DURING ALL HOURS OF OPERATION INCLUDING DURING PREPARATION. CONSIDER HAVING ANOTHER EMPLOYEE OBTAIN CERTIFICATION.

out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Records, Parasite Destruction, Farm-Raised
violations.observation: The following farm-raised fish served raw or partially cooked were observed without a written statement from the supplier stating that the fish were raised and fed according to 3-402.11(B)(3): OBSERVED NO PARASITE DESTRUCTION LETTER WAS AVAILABLE FOR SALMON SERVED UNDERCOOKED OR RAW IN SUSHI AND SASHIMI DISHES
violations.corrective_action: Contact your fish supplier and ask for a written statement stating that the fish were raised in net pens if in open water OR land-based operations AND fed formulated feed that contains no live parasites. FAX a copy of this letter to your inspector and keep this statement on site at the food establishment for 90 days beyond the time of service of the fish. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO REQUEST PARASITE DESTRUCTION LETTER FOR SALMON FROM SUPPLIER. DO NOT SERVE SALMON UNDERCOOKED OR RAW UNTIL PARASITE DESTRUCTION LETTER IS PROVIDED. PIC REQUESTED PARASITE DESTRUCTION LETTER FROM SUPPLIER BEFORE INSPECTION ENDED.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 70F, No More than 2 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours. RICE AT 84F FOR 4 HOURS IN COVERED PLASTIC DEEP CONTAINER IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO DISCARD FOODS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE COOKED FOODS ARE COOLED FROM 135F TO 70F IN 2 HOURS AND TO A FURTHER 41F WITHIN A TOTAL OF 6 HOURS.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: RICE PREPARED FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS WITHOUT DATE MARKING IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC APPLIED DATED LABEL DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE ALL FOODS PREPARED AND HELD FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS ARE DATE MARKED WITH DATE OF PREPARATION AND UNUSED PORTIONS DISCARDED AFTER 7 DAYS.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: RICE AT 84F FOR 4 HOURS IN DEEP COVERED CONTAINER IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO DISCARD RICE DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE USE SHALLOW PANS, SMALLER PORTIONS IN THE REFRIGERATOR OR FREEZER TO RAPIDLY COOL FOODS WITHIN THE PROPER PARAMETERS. DO NOT COVER FOODS UNTIL COOLED TO 41F OR BELOW.
